subject: Measurement protocol handoff / qualification recap for latency & streaming
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Measurement protocol handoff / qualification recap for latency & streaming

Hi Sam — great call earlier, thank you for walking us through Acme's traffic patterns and the streaming/checkout use case. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same handoff for the performance qualification run.

What we captured on the call:
- Targets: p95 latency <= 200ms for single-token streaming responses under normal traffic; p99 <= 450ms for end-to-end streaming (client-side aggregation).
- Concurrency envelope: steady-state 120 concurrent sessions, peak 400 concurrent during promo bursts (3–5 minute window).
- Throughput: 600 tokens/sec sustained across the pool during steady state; bursts up to 3k tokens/sec.
- Streaming semantics: partial tokens emitted every ~80–120ms; client aborts are common and KV cache reuse per session is important.

Action items (owners):
1) Acme (Sam) to share: canonical prompt set (20 canonical customer checkout flows + 10 edge cases), current latency targets spreadsheet, and a sample trace from prod (anonymized). (Sam)
2) Redwood to propose measurement protocol and harness config (what we will measure, how we inject concurrency, warmup, sampling windows, and pass/fail criteria). (Marissa + Vivek)
3) Decide whether to run a streaming-focused probe vs. a full throughput run first; propose running a streaming probe as priority given business risk. (All)

Attachments: I attached the template spreadsheet we usually use for target capture; please replace the placeholders with your measured values if available.

Thanks — I'll draft the measurement protocol and share a first-pass today.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — good recap and appreciate the clear AIs. Attaching our measured targets and a short doc that describes how our checkout clients open streams and aggregate partial tokens.

Notes / clarifications from our side:
- The p95 200ms target is per-token emission on the client side after Redwood's first chunk. End-to-end (app-visible) p95 is roughly +30–60ms network + client processing.
- Peak concurrency counts are per-region (we run US-east + US-west), the 400 number is per-region during Black Friday-style campaigns. For the qualification run we suggest profiling the worst-case region first (US-east).
- We can provide a sampled anonymized trace; it has headers that identify session IDs — we will scrub PII.

I've attached: acme_latency_targets.xlsx and acme_streaming_requirements.pdf. Also dropping a link to a shared Drive folder with the prompt bundle we have for this use case.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqX-ACME-Perf-Harness

Subject: Re: Measurement protocol handoff / qualification recap for latency & streaming

Sam / Marissa — thanks for the artifacts, I looked through the streaming requirements PDF and the targets spreadsheet. A couple of practical items I want to lock down before we schedule the probe: 

Measurement definitions (proposed) — please confirm these map to your expectations:
- Emission latency: time from Redwood server write-to-socket for first byte of chunk until client receives it (we will simulate network latency + client processing separately).
- Per-token latency: median/p95/p99 for single token emission when model is in steady-state (>30s after warmup).
- End-to-end streaming: measured from request start until 'final chunk' event; note that this metric is sensitive to client-side aggregation thresholds (we will align with your SDK team on the aggregation window).
- Throughput measurement: tokens/sec aggregated across all worker processes after steady-state; we will report token/s and requests/s.

Probe config suggestions (initial):
- Warmup: 5 minutes at 20% of target concurrency with KV cache prefill using the 'session seed' prompts you provide.
- Steady window: 10 minutes at target concurrency (120) for baseline; 10 minutes at 400 for peak simulation.
- Sampling: collect 1s granularity histograms and retain full traces for any p99 breaches.
- Reproducibility: we will version the prompt pack (git tag) and seed the harness RNG; please provide a canonical prompt bundle and indicate which prompts are deterministic vs. nondeterministic (we recommend marking any prompts that call external tools or include timestamps).

A couple of asks for Acme to enable a reproducible run:
1) Drop the prompt bundle in the Drive folder with a README that maps prompt ID -> expected behavior.
2) Indicate sample distribution of session lengths (median, 75th, 95th percentile) so we can model session hold times correctly.
3) Confirm whether KV caches are per-session or shared across session groups; this affects cache hit modeling.

I'll draft the exact harness config (runner.yml) and push to our shared drive; Marissa will share the runner parameters and the pass/fail matrix.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
